course_description: Study of fundamental data structures, recursive algorithms, dynamic memory, sorting, trees, and algorithmic complexity.

course_outcomes.co_description: Implement linear and non-linear data structures using appropriate dynamic memory management techniques.
Analyze time and space complexity of algorithms using Big-O notation to evaluate efficiency.
Design recursive algorithms to solve complex computational problems involving tree structures.
Develop optimized sorting and searching strategies for large datasets within system constraints.

weekly_schedule.topic: Introduction to Data Structures & Abstract Data Types

llos.outcome_text: Explain the differences between linear and non-linear data structures.
Implement array-based list operations and dynamic memory allocation.
Demonstrate precision in memory management and pointer debugging.

weekly_schedule.teaching_learning_activity: Hands-on coding lab on dynamic memory and pointers

weekly_schedule.topic: Linked Lists and Dynamic Memory Management

llos.outcome_text: Identify the structural differences between arrays and linked lists.
Construct singly and doubly linked list structures in memory.
Show responsibility in managing node creation and deallocation.
Describe the LIFO and FIFO principles in data structures.
Implement stack push/pop and queue enqueue/dequeue operations.
Apply ethical coding standards during implementation.
Explain the concept of base cases and recursive calls.
Write recursive functions to solve factorial and Fibonacci problems.
Demonstrate patience in debugging infinite recursion loops.
Define Big-O notation and its significance in algorithm efficiency.
Calculate time complexity for given algorithmic steps.
Analyze resource usage critically against performance metrics.
Compare various sorting algorithms like Bubble, Quick, and Merge Sort.
Implement optimized sorting strategies for large datasets.
Evaluate system constraints during algorithm selection.
Demonstrate understanding of linear and non-linear data structures.
Execute correct algorithmic logic under exam conditions.
Maintain academic integrity during the examination process.

weekly_schedule.teaching_learning_activity: Departmental Midterm Practical and Theoretical Exam
weekly_schedule.evidence: Examination Paper and Practical Code Submission

llos.outcome_text: Identify tree structures including binary search trees.
Implement in-order, pre-order, and post-order traversals.
Showcase professional code organization for tree structures.
Explain the properties of AVL and Red-Black trees.
Balance tree structures to maintain logarithmic height.
Apply optimization techniques for memory efficiency.
Differentiate between directed and undirected graphs.
Implement BFS and DFS traversal algorithms on graphs.
Demonstrate problem-solving skills in graph pathfinding.
Analyze the performance of Merge and Quick Sort variants.
Develop optimized sorting strategies for system constraints.
Ensure code efficiency meets project requirements.
Explain hash functions and collision resolution techniques.
Implement hash tables with chaining or open addressing.
Evaluate data structure efficiency in real-time systems.

weekly_schedule.evidence: Hash Table Source Code and Test Cases

llos.outcome_text: Synthesize knowledge of data structures for project design.
Integrate multiple algorithms into a cohesive system.
Demonstrate teamwork and professional collaboration skills.
Synthesize understanding of all data structures and algorithms.
Defend the final project architecture and algorithmic choices.
Demonstrate professional communication under pressure.
